label: Manor house
notes: a stone hall for the steward: rents are collected in full, the yard can be held, and a lord in residence settles the villages (owner 2026-09-13: build_days is how long the work takes at one day a step; the *_per_tick columns are what a finished building adds to the crown's metrics each tick; church_bonus is church_opinion per tick; produce_good/units join the ECONOMY column) civil_cost is what the work takes in CIVIL GOODS — the one price the game charges: MANOR_BUILD spends it, manor_demolish_refund returns a share of it to the stores, and it is the buildings' term in a manor's value. cost_gold is UNUSED by the game and kept for the library: hurrying is priced at build_rush_gold_per_day per day, so a full rush costs build_days x that.

label: Mill
notes: a water or wind mill: the manor grinds its own grain, takes a toll on its neighbours', and sends flour to the royal granaries

label: Granary
notes: a stone granary: the harvest keeps, and a bad year is survived

label: Chapel
notes: a chapel with its own priest: the pulpit speaks well of the house that built it

label: Palisade
notes: a ditch and timber wall around the yard: a raid has to work for it, and the villages sleep easier

label: Market
notes: a weekly market by charter: tolls and stall rents, and cloth changes hands
